status: Focused integration and native API passed; immutable installed acceptance running
scope: Twelve reproducible Irelia decision positions with an explicit legal solution, both seats and three AI levels
Wait for a lone friendly Irelia reset while continuing to consider an opposing response
Choose an exhausted unit that can reach the final unopposed scoring field, with actual spell and Ready payment validation
Beginner and Advanced commentary explains pending reset timing and updates when the opponent responds

checks.companion_scope: Both advice levels in the human seat, brief/read-only/private-safe; explicit pending-reset and enemy-response messages. No human learnability claim.

native_api.limits: These nine match traces are unchanged. New winning-route decisions are demonstrated by the authored benchmark, not inferred from these complete-match records.

comparison.result: Each of these four sequences failed in both seats for Easy and Tactical before the policy changes, and now succeeds. Strategic already completed them.
comparison.oracle_correction: Open-turn positions initially only required a win. Their final objective also requires preserving hand and resources. Do not compare the original overall percentage with the stricter final percentage.
comparison.fixture_correction: The enemy-response regression now explicitly passes after the enemy plays Gust; the caster retains priority. The initial test stepped the enemy a second time and incorrectly labeled that as an ignored response. No engine rule was changed.

limitations: Authored midgames are not complete legal-deck replays or independent proof of general rules parity.
The scored sequences assume a passing opponent; this is a development benchmark, not held-out or human-strength validation.
Easy and Tactical still pay for the empty-hand reset in this benchmark and spend cards during a winning showdown. Their measured result is 18/24 each; Strategic is 24/24.
The heuristic follow-up handles positive Might spells from hand and at most twelve candidate payments; other ready engines retain existing policy.
Timing includes step execution and was measured with another release job active; there is no speedup or maximum-latency guarantee.
The broader 173-test run preceded an equivalent lint rewrite from own_score + 1 <= enemy_score to own_score < enemy_score; both final benchmark tests and strict Clippy passed afterward.

rules_review.interpretation: A redundant Ready adds no Ready event; the authored winning line scores the other battlefield before attempting the final conquest. No game legality changes are included.

remaining: Inspect immutable full package, simulation and installed UI/API results
